title: Quarter Compass: Dedicated Capacity & Adaptive Burst Q3 Roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Quarterly roadmap artifact to align PM/Eng/Infra on the prioritized initiatives for Dedicated capacity and adaptive burst behavior for the coming quarter. Objective is to deliver predictable SLAs while reducing unit cost under bursty workloads by combining pre-warm corridors, fast fallback targets, and smarter burst orchestration. This ticket captures outcomes, milestones, acceptance criteria, resource needs, and the coordination plan with Dedicated SRE, Runtime, and Sales Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Defined Q3 outcomes and top-level success metrics (SLO attainment, cost/unit, mean cold-start latency)
Runbooks for two burst scenarios (inter-region surge, unexpected traffic spike) with verified canary playbooks
Implementation plan for adaptive-burst orchestrator MVP: scheduling policy, cost caps, and rollback mechanism
Cross-team sign-off (Runtime, Dedicated Ops, Console, Sales Eng) on rollout gating and A/B criteria
Telemetry dashboards created for per-route burst metrics and cost attribution
milestones: 2026-02-20: Strategy kickoff and hypothesis mapping completed
2026-02-28: Draft OKRs and experiment plan shared with stakeholders
2026-03-08: Prototype adaptive-burst scheduler policy defined (scheduling knobs + safety limits)
2026-03-22: Canary run 1 (internal traffic) and dashboard validation
2026-04-05: Canary run 2 (select customers) and post-mortem decisions
2026-04-18: Final rollout plan and handoff to Dedicated Ops
okrs: O1: Improve Dedicated pool SLA predictability for bursty tenants
KR1.1: Reduce 95th percentile request latency during burst by 25% vs baseline
KR1.2: Maintain pool availability > 99.95% across two burst scenarios
O2: Reduce marginal token cost during burst while preserving quality
KR2.1: Decrease per-token cost during sustained 3x traffic by 15%
KR2.2: No customer-visible drop in output quality for top 10 customers (monitored via eval prompt sets)
tasks: Define adaptive-burst policy language (policy schema + default profiles)
Prototype scheduler hook in runtime to accept burst policy signals
Implement cost-cap enforcement and graceful degradation path
Add telemetry: burst windows, warm-pool utilization, cold-start counts
Create canary playbook and define success/failure thresholds
Coordinate quota and billing team to model cost attribution for burst credits
Prepare customer communication templates and opt-in flow for piloting
risks: Risk: Overly aggressive pooling can increase baseline spend — mitigated by cost caps and daily burn alerts
Risk: Scheduler changes could increase tail latency if KV cache invalidation is not handled correctly — mitigate with small canaries and KV warm-path checks
Risk: Customers may opt out of pilot due to privacy/compliance concerns — mitigate by offering VPC-only pilot and clear data handling docs
Risk: Insufficient observability for per-route attribution — mitigate by shipping minimal telemetry ahead of canary
stakeholders: Maya Chen — Head of Dedicated Operations
Design: Priya Shah — UX for opt-in flows
